note: REAL verifier output, confirmed by running reference/standalone/verify_envelope.py, impl/go/cmd/scpe-verify, and impl/rust's scpe-verify binary (all three agree). Top-level "spec_version" is repeated: first occurrence (visually, at the top of the file) is the supported scpe/0.1; a duplicate "spec_version": "scpe/9.9" is appended as the manifest's LAST top-level key. All three implementations silently resolve the duplicate to the LAST occurrence (stdlib JSON last-key-wins in Python/Go/Rust here) and correctly reject THAT value as unsupported-version -- so no implementation was fooled into treating this manifest as verified. FLAG: RFC 8259 leaves duplicate-key handling implementation-defined; nothing in SPEC.md requires rejecting a manifest with duplicate top-level keys, and no verifier here does. That the three ports happen to agree (all last-wins) is a property of their JSON libraries' shared convention, not something the SCPE spec pins down -- a hypothetical fourth implementation using a first-wins or error-on-duplicate JSON parser could reach a DIFFERENT verdict on these exact signed bytes. This is a real cross-implementation ambiguity worth the spec/threat-model owner's attention, not a bug in any one verifier.
